title: A Sigil for the Spire Again
premise: Rafael Villalobos has spent nine years guarding the Thornfell gate and pretending she has no past, but when the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, a stranger arrives carrying her own forgotten memories in a locked box. She learns that nine years ago she sold her soul to the court beneath the mountain to seal the gate—and the price is now due. Descending through smugglers' roads into the subterranean court, Rafael must choose between reclaiming her soul and leaving it behind to keep the gate shut forever. In the end she shatters the bargain itself, binding the gate to her living memory rather than her soul, and steps back into a world where the stars return one by one.
about_author: Oscar Eriksen is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across northern Europe before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, personal, and otherwise—from a farmhouse overlooking a valley they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On a routine patrol of the Thornfell gate, the wards fail and every star vanishes at once; by dawn, a scarred stranger named Ivet stands at her door holding a locked box that hums with Rafael's own voice. The chapter establishes her careful, invisible life and ends with the box opening unbidden, flooding her with a memory of signing something in blood. Emotional beat: dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: What the Box Remembered
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with an interlude from Ivet's journal. The recovered memories reveal the truth: nine years ago Rafael sold her soul to the court beneath the mountain to seal the gate, then paid a hedge-witch to erase herself. With twelve of thirteen moon-turns already spent, she and Ivet take the smugglers' roads downward while the court's collectors close in. Emotional beat: grief for a self she chose to lose, hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the candlelit court beneath the mountain, Rafael confronts the Broker who holds her soul in a glass reliquary—and discovers Ivet was the one who guided her to the bargain long ago, loyalty entangled with betrayal. Offered her soul back in exchange for opening the gate, Rafael pretends to accept, then seizes the reliquary as the court erupts. Emotional beat: betrayal and fury igniting into desperate action—the climax begins.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Spire
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Fleeing upward with the reliquary cracking in her hands, Rafael realizes a stolen soul cannot simply be worn again. At the spire atop the gate, she carves a new sigil binding the ward not to her soul but to her living memory—every road, every name, every loss—accepting that she will remember everything forever. The stars return; Ivet leaves or stays, her choice made honest at last. Emotional beat: costly peace, identity reclaimed on her own terms.
